text:
alex: quick heads-up — on staging we've got steady RSS growth under long-context load when continuous batching is enabled. attaching flamegraph and a short log snippet. :eyes:

neha: repro steps?

alex: loadgen config: long_ctx=8k, contbatch=true, merge_window=50ms. after ~30m RSS climbs ~4-6GB. logs show frequent kv-evict + batch-merge stall entries. flamegraph: https://perf.internal/redwood/frag-2876543210 (private)

sam: can you paste a minimal log snippet from the window where RSS climbs?

alex: sure — pasted below:
```log
[12:02:11] batch-merge: id=0x7ff delay=12ms head=0x2 tail=0x8
[12:02:11] kv-evict: slab=23 freed=64KB
[12:02:12] batch-merge: stall reason=hol_spinlock
[12:02:13] kv-evict: slab=23 freed=32KB
[12:02:15] kv-reclaim: scanned=1024 live=980
[12:02:17] batch-merge: id=0x8b2 delay=45ms head=0x5
```

neha: hol_spinlock? that's a new knob in the logs — I thought we only had hol_block and merge-wait. :thinking_face:

sanjay: my guess: contbatch merge is holding onto KV refs while it serializes/merges heads, which prevents eviction from reclaiming fragments. repeated merges pin fragments and cause fragmentation growth + evict thrash.

alex: profiling (perf + eBPF) points to kv_slot_lock_holder in contbatch_merge_loop as the top CPU path during the stall window. flamegraph shows a tall stack at runtime::contbatch::merge -> runtime::kv::hold_ref -> kv::slot_lock.

perf-bot: perf alert: contbatch merge P95 latency increased 3.2x vs baseline (2026-03-17). suspect interaction with kv-residency increase.

sam: quick experiment — I toggled merge coalescing (merge_threshold=0) on staging and replayed the same load. RSS stayed flat for the same duration but p95 latency increased ~18%. so merging helps latency but seems to amplify KV residency.

neha: so it's a tradeoff: merge gives throughput/latency wins but at the cost of pinning KV fragments and creating long-lived allocations under long contexts. we need a middle ground.

sanjay: proposed quick mitigation: add merge backpressure based on a kv_free watermark. pseudocode:
```diff
@@ -320,6 +320,12 @@
- if (can_merge(batch, next)) merge(batch, next);
+ if (kv_free() < KV_WATERMARK) {
+   throttle_merge(); // drop coalescing, let batches go out independently
+ } else {
+   if (can_merge(batch,next)) merge(batch, next);
+ }
```
this should reduce the number of held refs during high-residency periods. also add metric merge_throttled_count.

alex: implemented a quick staging patch with throttle_merge gated behind a feature flag. initial soak (1h) looks promising — RSS slope flattened. will add metrics and run longer soak.

neha: longer-term: can we make merge non-blocking/optimistic so it doesn't hold slot locks across multiple fragments? maybe optimistic CAS + retry on conflict. could avoid hol_spinlock.

sanjay: that's doable but complex — need careful correctness on KV ref lifetimes. also consider releasing KV refs earlier in merge path (fast-path) so eviction has a chance.

sam: also add histogram for kv-residency by slab and for merge_hold_time. helps correlate which slabs are hot and for how long they're pinned.

alex: will open PR with the backpressure patch + metrics. planning a canary run (2% prod) with merge_throttle enabled and capture kv-residency histograms and merge_hold_time.

perf-bot: action item created: PERF-1428 (run canary, collect kv-residency histo, compare merge_throttled_count).

neha: cool. if canary looks good we can tune merge_window and KV_WATERMARK to regain some latency without the memory penalty.

alex: thanks — sending link to PR once it's up.

sanjay: fyi, if anyone else sees hol_spinlock in logs, add the tag `hol_spinlock` to the thread — helps grep across clusters.

sam: ack.

alex: PR link: https://git.internal/redwood/contbatch/pull/432 (draft) — includes canary flag + metrics + short-term throttle. will update after soak. :thumbsup:
